title: Food Chains and Food Webs
seo_title: Grade 5 Food Web Worksheets: Producers, Consumers, Food Chains and Ecosystems
standard_text: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on food chains and food webs (NGSS 5-LS2-1): producers, herbivores, carnivores, omnivores and decomposers, reading arrows, and what happens when a population changes. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Arrows in a food web point from the food to the eater.
key_sub: Every food chain starts with a producer. Matter and energy move along the arrows, and a change in one population affects the whole web.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every food chain starts with a producer (a plant or algae) that makes its own food using sunlight. Consumers get matter and energy by eating: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals and omnivores eat both. Decomposers break down dead organisms.

Arrows point from the food to the eater, in the direction matter and energy move. Many food chains that connect make a food web.

Example

In the meadow web, what does the snake eat?

Find the arrows that point to the snake.

They come from the mouse and the frog.

Answer: mice and frogs

Example

If most of the grasshoppers died, which animal would lose its only food?

The frog eats only grasshoppers.

The mouse also eats wildflowers, so it has other food.

Answer: the frog

Common mistakes

  • Reading the arrow as “eats”: grass → rabbit means the rabbit eats the grass.
  • Thinking only the animal that eats the lost organism is affected. Changes spread through the whole web.
  • Forgetting that every food chain starts with a producer and that its energy first came from the sun.

faq.q: What is the difference between a food chain and a food web?
faq.a: A food chain shows one path of food, like grass → rabbit → fox. A food web shows many connected food chains in an ecosystem.

faq.q: Which way do the arrows point in a food web?
faq.a: From the food to the eater. They show the direction matter and energy move.

faq.q: What are producers, consumers and decomposers?
faq.a: Producers make their own food from sunlight. Consumers eat other organisms. Decomposers break down dead organisms and return matter to the soil.

faq.q: What happens if one animal disappears from a food web?
faq.a: Animals that eat it may lose food and decrease, and the organisms it ate may increase. The change can spread through the whole web.

sets.title: What happens when a population changes?

items.q: Use the desert food web. Most of the hawks are removed from the desert. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the hawk eats rattlesnakes. With fewer predators, more rattlesnakes survive.

items.e: Only the frog eats dragonflys. With fewer predators, more dragonflys survive.

c: Most animals eat more than one kind of food, and a web shows all the links.
